answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable stake locked when the agent first joins. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, so a Sybil flood becomes expensive instead of free. Peers only attest identities that held their stake through real work, and a jade-grade reputation is earned slowly, like climbing toward a summit, while misbehaviour slashes the stake. Honest agents pay once; attackers must pay again and again.
